mainTopic: A person who says "הריני נזיר" but then adds "from dried figs and fig cakes": the מחלוקת between בית שמאי and בית הלל about whether he becomes a נזיר
overview: The משנה brings a case where someone says "I am a נזיר from dried figs and fig cakes," even though a נזיר is only forbidden in grape products. בית שמאי say he is a full נזיר, and בית הלל say he is not a נזיר at all. רבי יהודה narrows בית שמאי's view: they only meant that the figs become forbidden to him, like a קרבן. The גמרא first explains that בית שמאי follow רבי מאיר (a person does not speak for nothing). It explains that בית הלל follow רבי יוסי (a person is held to the end of his words, so this is a נדר ופתחו עמו). But that reasoning would apply to בית שמאי too, so the גמרא gives a new explanation. For בית שמאי, "I am a נזיר" takes hold at once, and the figs part is a request to cancel the vow. That request fails, because they hold there is no שאלה for הקדש, and so none for נזירות either. בית הלל are now explained through רבי שמעון: a vow made in a way no one ever vows has no effect.

steps.title: The case: a נזיר vow tied to dried figs
steps.stepSummary: The משנה presents a person who says he is a נזיר from dried figs and fig cakes. בית שמאי say he is a נזיר, and בית הלל say he is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says, "I am a נזיר from dried figs and fig cakes," בית שמאי say he is a נזיר, and בית הלל say he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with a strange vow. A person uses the words of נזירות but attaches them to figs, which have nothing to do with being a נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר is forbidden in grape products, not in figs. So the person's two phrases clash: "I am a נזיר" points to נזירות, but "from figs" points somewhere else. בית שמאי keep the first part and make him a נזיר, while בית הלל say no נזירות takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: "I am hereby a נזיר," the standard words for taking on נזירות
Dried figs
A cake made of pressed dried figs
The two great schools of תנאים who often disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Figs are NOT forbidden to a נזיר. That is the whole puzzle: the man linked נזירות to something that has nothing to do with נזירות.

phrases.english: "I am hereby a nazir
from dried figs and from fig cakes"
phrases.notes: A נזיר is only forbidden in grape products, so tying the vow to figs makes no sense on its face.

phrases.english: Beis Shammai say: he is a nazir.
And Beis Hillel say: he is not a nazir.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר מִן הַגְּרוֹגְרוֹת וּמִן הַדְּבֵילָה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: he is a נזיר. בית הלל: he is not a נזיר.

steps.title: רבי יהודה narrows בית שמאי's view
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה explains that בית שמאי only meant the figs become forbidden to him, as if he said "they are a קרבן to me."
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה said: even when בית שמאי said this, they only meant it in a case where the person says, "These figs are forbidden to me like a קרבן."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה gives a different reading of what בית שמאי meant. In his view, בית שמאי were not talking about real נזירות at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי יהודה, the vow works only as a ban on the figs, the way a person can forbid food to himself by calling it a קרבן. So בית שמאי make the figs forbidden but do not make him a real נזיר. This changes the מחלוקת from "is he a נזיר?" into "are the figs forbidden?"

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who here gives his own reading of בית שמאי
"They are hereby upon me as a קרבן," a phrase that forbids an item to oneself
An offering; used in vows to forbid something like an offering is forbidden

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda said:
Even when Beis Shammai said it,
they only said it about one who says
"They are hereby upon me as a korban."
phrases.notes: He means: the figs become forbidden to him, the way an offering is forbidden for ordinary use.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אַף כְּשֶׁאָמְרוּ בֵּית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits and reinterprets בית שמאי's ruling in step 1
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי only meant that the figs become forbidden as a קרבן, not real נזירות.

steps.title: Why would בית שמאי make him a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes בית שמאי's ruling and asks how he can be a נזיר, since the תורה limits נזירות to grape products.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא quotes the משנה: "I am a נזיר from dried figs and fig cakes," בית שמאי say he is a נזיר. But why? The תורה says a נזיר is forbidden "from anything made from the grapevine"!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges בית שמאי. Figs are not part of נזירות, so how can a vow about figs make someone a נזיר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק defines נזירות by grape products only. The man spoke about figs, so his words should not fit נזירות at all. The question is how בית שמאי can ignore the "figs" part and give him full נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains and analyzes the משנה
"But why?" a challenge to a ruling
"From the grapevine," the limit of what a נזיר may not eat
"The Merciful One," meaning the תורה‎ / ה׳

phrases.english: Gemara
"I am hereby a nazir from dried figs and from fig cakes" —
Beis Shammai say: he is a nazir.
But why?
"From anything that is made from the grapevine"
the Merciful One said!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַמַּאי? מִכֹּל אֲשֶׁר יֵעָשֶׂה מִגֶּפֶן הַיַּיִן אָמַר רַחֲמָנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Re-quotes the משנה from step 1 in order to challenge בית שמאי
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's ruling that he is a נזיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק limits נזירות to grape products, so a vow about figs should not create נזירות.

steps.title: בית שמאי follow רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי hold like רבי מאיר, who says a person does not say words for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי hold like רבי מאיר, who said: a person does not say his words for nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by linking בית שמאי to a known principle of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the man said "I am a נזיר," those words must mean something, so we do not throw them away. Since "from figs" cannot work as נזירות, we assume he really meant to become a נזיר and the figs part was a mistake. That is why he becomes a full נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: "They hold like...", meaning they follow that view
A תנא whose principle is quoted here
A person does not say words for nothing; his words are given meaning

phrases.english: Beis Shammai hold
like Rabbi Meir, who said:
A person does not utter his words for nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the ruling to a known principle of another תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since figs are not part of נזירות, the vow should be meaningless.
steps.terutzMaskana: His words "I am a נזיר" are not thrown away, so he becomes a נזיר.

steps.title: בית הלל follow רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל hold like רבי יוסי, who says a person is held to the end of his words, so this vow comes with its own way out.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל hold like רבי יוסי, who said: a person is caught by the end of his words. And this is a vow that carries its own opening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now explains בית הלל's side, again by linking them to a known principle, this time of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי says we must also take seriously the last part of what a person says. Here the last part, "from figs," shows he never meant real נזירות. So the vow undoes itself from inside, a נדר ופתחו עמו, and he is not a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא whose principle is quoted here
A person is held to the end of his words too
A vow that carries its own "opening," a built-in reason it does not take hold

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי = רבי מאיר: the first words count, so he is a נזיר. בית הלל = רבי יוסי: the last words count too, so the vow cancels itself (נדר ופתחו עמו).

phrases.english: And Beis Hillel hold
like Rabbi Yosei, who said:
A person is held by the end of his words.
And this is a vow with its opening along with it.
phrases.notes: The "opening" is the figs part: it shows from inside the vow that he never meant real נזירות.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer by explaining the other side of the מחלוקת
steps.terutzResolutionType: Ties the opposing ruling to a contrary principle of another תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps the words "I am a נזיר" should take hold no matter what follows.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ending "from figs" counts too, so the vow cancels itself and he is not a נזיר.

steps.title: Isn't it a self-cancelling vow for בית שמאי too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בית שמאי: even by their view, this should be a נדר ופתחו עמו that does not take hold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And for בית שמאי too, this is a vow that carries its own opening!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer for בית שמאי. The idea of נדר ופתחו עמו seems true no matter whose principle you follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if the first words are not thrown away, the figs part is still right there in the vow, showing he did not mean real נזירות. A vow that contains its own way out should not take hold for anyone. So how can בית שמאי say he is a נזיר? The next step answers this with a new reading of בית שמאי.

keyTerms.meaning: "Also / too"

phrases.english: And for Beis Shammai too,
it is a vow with its opening along with it!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי נָמֵי, נֶדֶר וּפִתְחוֹ עִמּוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reasoning given for בית הלל in step 5 to attack the answer for בית שמאי in step 4
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that בית שמאי follow רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The vow has its own built-in reason not to take hold, so even בית שמאי should agree he is not a נזיר.

steps.title: A new explanation: his words about figs are an attempt to cancel the vow
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets aside the earlier explanation. By רבי מאיר's rule, saying "I am a נזיר" makes him a נזיר at once, and adding "from dried figs" is an attempt to get out of the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: בית שמאי hold like רבי מאיר, who said a person does not say words for nothing. So once he said "I am a נזיר," he became a נזיר. When he then adds "from dried figs and from fig cakes," he is trying to get his vow cancelled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 6 with a new way of reading בית שמאי. The words "I am a נזיר" take hold right away, and the part about figs is just him trying to back out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 6 argued that the whole sentence should count as one vow that comes with its own way out, so it would never take hold. The new answer breaks the sentence into two parts. The first part already made him a נזיר, and the second part is a separate attempt to undo it, like asking a חכם to cancel a vow.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. The גמרא is dropping the earlier answer and giving a new one.
He has become a נזיר, right away
To request that a חכם cancel a vow (שאלה)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר was already mentioned in step 4, but here his rule leads somewhere new. The point now is that the figs part is a request to cancel the vow. It is no longer read as part of the vow itself.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר,
phrases.english: Rather: בית שמאי hold like רבי מאיר,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵין אָדָם מוֹצִיא דְּבָרָיו לְבַטָּלָה.
phrases.english: who said: a person does not say his words for nothing.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר ״הֲרֵינִי נָזִיר״ — הֲוָה לֵיהּ נָזִיר,
phrases.english: And once he said "I am hereby a נזיר," he became a נזיר.
When he goes on to say "from dried figs and from fig cakes,"
he is coming to have the vow cancelled.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי סָבְרִי לַהּ כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 6 by replacing the earlier explanation of בית שמאי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the case: the statement is split into a vow that already took hold, followed by a request to cancel it.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The whole sentence is one vow that carries its own way out, so it should never take hold.
steps.terutzMaskana: "I am a נזיר" takes hold at once, and "from dried figs" is a separate attempt to cancel it.

steps.title: Why the cancellation fails: no שאלה for הקדש or נזירות
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי follow their own known view that a vow of הקדש cannot be cancelled by a חכם. נזירות works the same way, so his attempt to cancel fails and he stays a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי follow their own reasoning, since they say a vow of הקדש cannot be cancelled. And since a vow of הקדש cannot be cancelled, a vow of נזירות cannot be cancelled either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer for בית שמאי. It explains why his request to cancel the vow does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 raises a question: if he is asking to cancel the vow, why not let him? The answer is that בית שמאי already hold elsewhere that a vow of הקדש cannot be cancelled. נזירות is treated like הקדש, so the נזירות stays in force.

keyTerms.meaning: Following their own known reasoning from somewhere else
Asking a חכם to cancel a vow
Property set aside as holy, for the בית המקדש
The state of being a נזיר

steps.whatToRemember: For בית שמאי, "I am a נזיר from figs" means he really is a נזיר. The figs part is a failed attempt to cancel the vow, because נזירות, like הקדש, cannot be cancelled.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the ruling here to a wider view of בית שמאי, that vows of holiness like הקדש and נזירות cannot be undone by שאלה.

phrases.english: And בית שמאי follow their own reasoning, for they say:
there is no cancelling a vow of הקדש.
And since there is no cancelling a vow of הקדש,
there is no cancelling a vow of נזירות.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes step 7 by explaining why the attempt to cancel the vow does not work.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing in another known position of the same opinion holder
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If he is asking to cancel the vow, maybe the cancellation should work and he would not be a נזיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: For בית שמאי, נזירות cannot be cancelled, just like הקדש, so he remains a נזיר.

steps.title: בית הלל follow רבי שמעון: an unusual vow means nothing
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל hold like רבי שמעון, who rules that someone who pledges in a way people never pledge is not obligated at all. Here too, a נזיר vow about figs means nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל hold like רבי שמעון. As we learned in a משנה: רבי שמעון exempts him, because he did not pledge the way people normally pledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now gives a new explanation for בית הלל, who said he is not a נזיר. It bases their view on a ruling of רבי שמעון from a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, in step 5, בית הלל were explained through רבי יוסי. Now they are linked to רבי שמעון instead. No one ever makes a נזיר vow about figs, just as no one ever pledges a מנחה made of barley. A vow made in such an odd way does not count, so he is completely free.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Exempts. Rules that the person has no obligation.
Pledged a voluntary gift
In the normal way people make pledges

steps.whatToRemember: בית שמאי (through רבי מאיר) say he is a נזיר and cannot cancel it. בית הלל (through רבי שמעון) say a vow made in a way no one vows means nothing.

phrases.english: And בית הלל hold like רבי שמעון,
as we learned: and רבי שמעון exempts him,
phrases.notes: This is from the משנה in מנחות 103a, about someone who pledged a מנחה made of barley instead of wheat.

phrases.english: because he did not pledge the way people pledge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes along with the new explanation of בית שמאי by giving a new source for בית הלל's view, in place of the רבי יוסי approach from step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Linking the opinion to a known תנא's rule from another משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: בית הלל's view rested on רבי יוסי's rule that a person is held to the end of his words.
steps.terutzMaskana: בית הלל follow רבי שמעון: a pledge made in a way no one pledges has no effect, so he is not a נזיר.
